issues.detail: The Greek 'επει ουκ αν επαυσαντο' (because they would not cease) is a causal statement explaining why something happens. The Vietnamese 'Nếu không... há chẳng thôi...' transforms this into a rhetorical question ('If not... would they not stop?'), changing the logical structure of the sentence.

The Greek uses the imperfect tense 'επαυσαντο' to describe a continuous action (ceasing/stopping). The Vietnamese phrasing obscures the continuous nature of the action by framing it as a hypothetical question.
